title: The Raven and the Swan

full_text:
A raven, observing a graceful swan gliding across a calm lake, became consumed with intense envy of the swan's dazzling white plumage. The raven concluded that the swan's snowy brilliance came solely from living in the clear water and washing its feathers every hour.

Abandoning his native woods, the raven took up residence in the marshes and lakes. From dawn to dusk, he bathed in the cold water, washing his feathers and rubbing his wings with river reeds.

He altered his diet to eat water weeds and pond moss instead of his natural food. But no amount of washing could lighten the pitch-black color of his feathers.

Within a month, unable to digest the watery marsh plants and chilled to the bone by constant immersion in the cold streams, the foolish raven grew weak and died of fever, proving that external habits cannot alter what nature has fundamentally designed.
moral: You cannot change your essential nature by altering your external environment.
